transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling Cardholder Services. My name is Marcus. Who do I have the pleasure of speaking with today?
Customer: Hi Marcus, this is Simone Okafor. I'm calling about an issue with a gym fee on my card.
Agent: Hello Ms. Okafor. I can look into that for you. May I first confirm the billing zip code on your account?
Customer: Sure, it's 75204.
Agent: Thank you. And could you also verify the last four digits of your card?
Customer: Yes, 8102.
Agent: Perfect, that verifies your account. Now, go ahead and tell me what happened with the gym.
Customer: Well, I used to go to Peakform Gym. I cancelled my membership with them at the end of August, and they took money out on August 31st.
Agent: Okay, Peakform Gym on August 31st. Did you speak with anyone there when that charge went through?
Customer: Yeah, I spoke with the manager. She told me they would refund the last month's dues back to my card.
Agent: Did they give you a timeframe for when that money should appear back on your account?
Customer: The person at the desk said it would take maybe seven to ten business days. But it’s been well over a month now, and I haven't seen a penny back.
Agent: Have you tried getting in touch with Peakform Gym again since that conversation?
Customer: I did. I called them a couple of weeks ago and left two voicemails, but nobody ever returned my calls.
Agent: Did they provide you with any cancellation receipt, email, or confirmation number at the time?
Customer: They gave me a printed cancellation form that showed my membership was ended, and the guy wrote on it that the dues would be returned.
Agent: Okay, so just to make sure I have all the details correct: you cancelled your membership at Peakform Gym, were charged on August 31st, they told you that they would return that final month of dues to your card within a couple of weeks, but nothing has shown up and they haven't responded to your follow-up calls.
Customer: Yes, exactly. That's the whole situation.
